newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Union, Bollore's ANZDL to form shipping venture.
newsitem.headline: Union, Bollore's ANZDL to form shipping venture.

text.p: Union Shipping, half owned by New Zealand's Brierley Investments Ltd (BIL), has formed a new shipping company with Australia New Zealand Direct Line to operate trans-Tasman and North American services, BIL said on Tuesday.
The move follows an agreement between BIL and Groupe Bollore Technologies, which owns ANZDL.

"Brierley will acquire a 50 percent stake in ANZDL and Bollore will acquire a 50 percent share of Union Shipping's trans-Tasman liner services. These business will be merged to form the new business which will be owned 50:50 by Brierley and
Bollore," a joint statement by BIL and Bollore said.

The agreement is conditional on regulatory approvals and BIL acquiring the half of Union Shipping currently owned by Australia's TNT Ltd. Once ratified, the new company is expected to start operations in early March.
BIL company secretary Mark Horton said arrangements with TNT should be concluded in the next couple of days. BIL would not disclose financial details.

The whole of ANZDL will be included in the new venture and ANZDL's present chief executive Michael Beard will remain as CEO. Horton said the rest of Union Shipping, apart from the trans-Tasman liner trade, will carry on under existing management and will be 100 percent owned by BIL.
Horton said the rationale for the move was to improve the direct line shipping services between the U.S. west coast, Australia and New Zealand.
